title: Monotonicity of random-string probability
statement: Let $m$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $A$ and $B$ be decidable properties of Boolean strings. If every Boolean string of length $m$ satisfying $A$ also satisfies $B$, then the probability that a uniformly random Boolean string of length $m$ satisfies $A$ is at most the probability that it satisfies $B$.
hypotheses_covered: $A$ and $B$ are decidable properties of Boolean strings
For every Boolean string $r$ of length $m$, $A(r)$ implies $B(r)$
